$description: Lattice-dashboard-only extension tokens: status LED colors (lat-led-*). Source: lattice_dashboard/static/dashboard.css lines 21-25. The dashboard currently ships ONE :root block only (no light theme at all — it is being brought into the fleet for the first time by this feature, per PLAN.md Task 3.6's 'full teal harmonization'). Decision: dark and light values are IDENTICAL here since there is no existing light-mode LED convention to preserve; these are small saturated status indicators (non-text UI, not WCAG-gated), so reusing the same value in both modes is a safe default. Task 3.6 (out of this task's scope) may revisit if the harmonization review flags LED legibility on the light background. ready/error/stale already coincide with existing ramp steps (green.400/red.300/amber.400); computing aliases the color.amber.250 ramp step added in core.json specifically for this value (#eab308); idle (#4a5264) is a genuinely new one-off literal with no matching slate step, kept as a literal rather than forcing an unused ramp insertion. The high-contrast family AUTHORS its own groups rather than inheriting: that family is fully monochrome, and an inherited saturated LED would be the one hue left on the page. The monochrome LEDs separate by lightness on the same ladder the high-contrast themes' status.* colors use (most urgent = furthest from the canvas), and the dashboard's LED labels carry the state name in text.

lat-led.$description: AUTHORED rather than inherited, for the same reason the high-contrast groups are: the `desy` family uses DESY Styleguide (06/24) hexes only, and inherited generic LEDs would be the only off-palette hues on the page. The state ladder keeps its conventional semantics with published colours — Green ready, Yellow computing, Red error, Olive stale, petrol neutral idle. These are small non-text indicators and are not WCAG-gated; the dashboard labels each LED with its state name in text.

stale.$description: DESY Olive — a desaturated warm hold state, distinct from the brighter Yellow used for computing.

idle.$description: Petrol neutral, replacing the one-off #4a5264 literal — idle is the absence of state, so it takes the canvas ramp.

lat-led.$description: AUTHORED rather than inherited — see the desy-dark group. The warm states move to the palette's dark half so they stay visible against a near-white canvas: DESY Yellow and Olive wash out there (1.47:1 / 1.91:1), so computing takes the accessibility orange and stale takes Dark olive.

computing.$description: DESY accessibility orange — DESY Yellow is invisible on this canvas.

error.$description: DESY Dark red — the palette's strongest red on light.

stale.$description: DESY Dark olive — the legible counterpart to the dark theme's Olive.

idle.$description: Petrol neutral at the light-canvas step.
